senses.gloss: ch. = h.צוּף [to shine,] to come to the surface, float, bubble up. Part. טָאֵיף, טָיֵיף.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 21:1">Targ. Y. Deut. XXI, 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 28:10">Targ. Y. Gen. XXVIII, 10</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:8:5">Koh. R. to V, 8</cite> (mixed diction) <he>וטָפַת בארה של וכ׳</he> Miriam’s well came up.—
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 2:6">Ab. II, 6</cite>; <cite ref="Sukkah 53a">Succ. 53ᵃ</cite>, v. infra.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 9:1:13">Y. Shebi. IX, 38ᵈ</cite>; Pesik. B’shall. p. 89ᵇ <he>הוה טָיֵיף</he> the corpse came up to the surface.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 81:2">Gen. R. s. 81</cite> (in Hebr. dict.) <he>וטָפַת רוחי וכ׳</he> and my mind in me was swimming (I became proud, v. <cite ref="I00636"><he>טָפַח</he></cite>); a. fr.

senses.gloss: (denom. of טיף) to drip; to be inundated.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 49:12">Targ. O. Gen. XLIX, 12</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Ketubot 111b:22">Keth. 111ᵇ</cite> <he>חלבא טייף וכ׳</he> milk was dripping &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 3:11:4">Y. Taan. III, end, 67ᵃ</cite> <he>הוה עלמא ט׳</he> the world would have been flooded.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 32">Gen. R. s. 32</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 57:2">Yalk. ib. 57</cite> <he>דלא טף וכ׳</he> it (the mount Gerizim) was not flooded by the waters of the flood; a. e.—[<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 21:23">Targ. Y. Deut. XXI, 23</cite> <he>תטופון</he>, v. <cite ref="I00582"><he>טְנַף</he></cite> a. <cite ref="N00578"><he>נְטַף</he></cite>.]

senses.gloss: to direct the overflow, to assign channels.
units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 38:24">Targ. Job XXXVIII, 24</cite>, v. <cite ref="I00410"><he>טְיָפָא</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Gittin 69b:1">Gitt. 69ᵇ</cite> top <he>ונִיטַּיְיפֵיה וכ׳</he> and let it (the milk) run over &c.

senses.gloss: to cause to glisten, to turn in all directions.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 60b">Keth. 60ᵇ</cite> <he>מְטַיְּפֵי עינא</he> Ar. (ed. <he>מציצי</he>, v. infra) with restless eyes.
<cite ref="Onkelos Deuteronomy 11:4">Targ. Deut. XI, 4</cite>.—[Keth. l. c. <he>מְטִיפֵי עינא</he> Ar. s. v. <cite ref="I00623"><he>טף</he></cite> I ‘with dripping eyes’, v. supra.]

Ab. II, 6 על דאֲטֵפְתְּ אֲטִיפוּךְ וסוף מְטִיפָיךְ יְטוּפוּן ed. Strack (oth. eds. אַטְפוּךְ; Strack reads מְטַיְפָיךְ Pa.; oth. pointed eds. מְטיְּפָיִךְ h. form) because thou (the person whose skull was seen to float) hast caused (a corpse) to float, they made thee float, and those who made thee float, shall also float.

senses.gloss: to be glittering, to be turned in all directions.
units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 92b">B. Kam. 92ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Megillah 14b">Meg. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>ועיניה מִטַּיְּיפֵי</he> and its eyes look all around (for food).
